Chapter 6: Releasing the Trap of Duty and Obligation
Have you ever caught yourself doing something, not because you genuinely wanted to, but simply because you felt you had to? Maybe it’s that sense of duty, or a nagging feeling of obligation—like you’re living out someone else’s expectations instead of your own.
These “shoulds” we carry around often sneak in from our families, our culture, or people we looked up to when we were younger. Before we know it, they quietly shape our choices. Life can start to feel kind of cramped, like we're following a script that wasn’t even written by us.
Here’s the heart of the matter: it’s so important to notice the difference between doing something because you freely choose it, and doing it out of guilt or the fear of letting someone down. When our actions are mostly driven by obligation, it’s no wonder we end up feeling tired—or even resentful.
Picture it like this: imagine carrying around a big, heavy coat in the middle of summer, just because someone once insisted you needed it. Eventually, that weight gets exhausting.
So, how do you start letting go of that grip duty can have? Here are a few ideas:
First, pay attention to moments when your decisions are led by “I have to” or “I should,” instead of a genuine “I want to.”
Next, ask yourself, “Whose rule is this, really? Does it actually fit with what I value or need?”
And finally, try saying “no” to things that don’t align with your own priorities. Notice what happens. Sometimes, the world doesn’t fall apart—and you might even feel lighter.
Think about someone who goes to every single family gathering—even when it leaves them stressed or forces them to put aside other things that matter. If they pause and question that old belief—like, “A good son or daughter always shows up”—they can start making choices that honor both their family and themselves.
Now, this isn’t about dropping all responsibility or turning into someone who only thinks about themselves. It’s about choosing from a place that’s real—a place where your actions reflect your true values and desires.
With this shift, you’ll notice more energy, more satisfaction, and a sense of integrity that comes from living authentically.
